mustFix.title: The exactly-at-preHandshake member requires an immediate RF-2 refusal for a prefix value the governing bound permits
mustFix.claimUnderReview: G21.cc5.prefix-exactly-at-prehandshake is the four-byte prefix 00010000 (N=65536) with no body, and the subject says the receiver must return RF-2 from the prefix alone and read no body.
primaryEvidence: The pinned control-protocol-contract.v2 $.transportAndFraming.framing.bounds.preHandshake says that N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0 is RF-2 from the prefix alone. Equality at 65536 is deliberately outside that prefix-only refusal predicate.
The fixture bytes recompute to 00 01 00 00, the four-byte big-endian unsigned value 65536. They therefore encode the maximum permitted preHandshake length, not an oversize length.

The same contract's RF-2 family includes truncated body. With a legal N=65536 prefix followed by EOF and zero body bytes, an eventual RF-2 can be attributed to truncation only after the receiver observes the missing body; it cannot lawfully be attributed to the prefix alone.
The subject reproduces the governing bound verbatim, so $.authoredCatalog.members[0].mutation and .expected directly contradict a source quoted on the subject's own evidence surface.
mustFix.impact: A receiver with the off-by-one defect N >= 65536 instead of N > 65536 would satisfy this expected result, while a conforming receiver that accepts the legal prefix and waits for its body could be failed for not refusing immediately. The member therefore cannot serve as correct retained conformance evidence for the exact-bound case. This is load-bearing fixture semantics, not editorial wording.
mustFix.requiredRemedy: Do not record this frozen v9. In a successor, either defer the exact-bound member until its delivery/session construction is pinned, or specify a test that requires the legal 65536 prefix to be accepted and distinguishes a later truncated-body/EOF RF-2 from prefix-only oversize refusal. Do not require RF-2 from the prefix alone for N=65536. Preserve the frozen fixture during repair unless a separately reviewed successor deliberately replaces its bytes.

mustFix.title: The remainder inventory drops the separately required postHandshake exactly-at and far-over variants
mustFix.claimUnderReview: The subject treats the leftover-join's generic exactly-at and far-over entries as authored by two explicitly preHandshake members, then lists only prefix one over the postHandshake bound among the remaining bound-edge injections.
primaryEvidence: The pinned control-protocol-contract.v2 CC-5 intent requires prefix exactly at, one over, and far over the operative bound with pre- and post-handshake bounds separately. The phase split is an explicit coverage quantifier.
Recorded g21-fixture-corpus.v7 authors only prefix one over preHandshake. The v9 member identifiers likewise end in prehandshake and its purpose says both new payloads are preHandshake cases.

No v9 field supplies postHandshake session state. The already-recorded OQ-G21-4 in DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md states that whether a postHandshake fixture needs a session script rather than a payload file is unresolved.

Despite that unresolved phase construction, $.remainderAfterThisCorpus enumerates postHandshake one-over but omits postHandshake exactly-at and far-over. $.whatIsNotAuthored and $.proposedLaterWork omit them too.
mustFix.coverageConstraint: D-293 Decision 8 delegates G21 fixture choices only under the agreed coverage constraints. Those constraints preserve every explicit mutation quantifier in the governing bytes. A preHandshake-only payload cannot silently consume a separately required postHandshake variant whose session context is not authored.
mustFix.impact: The artifact understates remaining CC-5 work and could cause a later leftover-join remasurement to erase two governing phase variants without any postHandshake witness or session construction. Keeping OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING open for other reasons does not make this accounting error harmless.
mustFix.requiredRemedy: A successor must retain postHandshake exactly-at and far-over in the not-authored/remainder inventory unless it pins a lawful session construction that demonstrates those variants. It must not treat the two preHandshake member ids as phase-independent coverage, and it should carry the existing OQ-G21-4 boundary rather than silently deciding it.
